fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions on the road.
• Mark the access drive entry point with reflective posts or markers so responders can locate it quickly at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so responders can reach the detached structure without obstruction.
• Post the property address at both the front driveway and the access drive if they enter from different points.
• Keep the walkway clear of stored items so responders can move between the main residence and detached structure on foot.
• Mark or label the detached structure on any posted site map so responders arriving at the front driveway know a second structure exists at the rear or side of the property.
• Keep gates along the access drive unlocked or secured with a Knox-style lock so responders are not delayed reaching the detached structure.
• Trim any landscaping along the access drive that narrows the travel width or obstructs sightlines for larger response vehicles.
• Designate and keep clear a flat, firm staging area near the front driveway large enough for a responding unit to park without blocking the access drive.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang close to the house or other structures.
• Thin scattered trees near structures to increase open space between them and the buildings.
• Remove shrubs that are growing directly against or immediately next to any structure.
• Separate shrub clusters from nearby trees by cutting or removing plants between them.
• Keep the area directly around each structure clear of loose dead leaves, branches, and plant debris.
• Maintain open ground between shrub groupings and structures so there is no continuous line of plants leading to a building.
• Keep all access routes free of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
